title: Commercial Jet Airliner
body:
Commercial Jet Airliner is a jet-powered passenger aircraft built for scheduled airline service, with a pressurised cabin, wing-mounted engines, and ranges from short hops to intercontinental flights. The Boeing 737, the best-selling jetliner in history, and the Airbus A320 family are the workhorses of this type.

Jet airliners shrank the world after the Second World War, making air travel ordinary and reshaping tourism, business, and migration.

title: Supersonic Transport
body:
Supersonic Transport is a jet airliner designed to cruise faster than sound, carrying passengers at Mach 2 across oceans. Concorde, flown by British Airways and Air France from 1976 to 2003, crossed the Atlantic in under four hours and remains the only supersonic airliner in sustained service.

Concorde is a public icon of aviation ambition, and its retirement closed the supersonic passenger era for a generation.

title: Business Jet
body:
Business Jet is a small jet aircraft built for corporate and private travel, carrying a handful of passengers point to point without airline schedules. Business jets such as the Learjet and the Gulfstream families serve executives, medical flights, and remote communities.

Business jets trade capacity for flexibility, reaching small airfields that airliners cannot serve.

title: Cargo Jet
body:
Cargo Jet is a jet aircraft built or converted to carry freight, with a large cargo door, a reinforced floor, and no passenger cabin. Cargo jets such as the Boeing 747 Freighter move high-value and urgent goods worldwide overnight.

Cargo jets are the express arm of global trade, and their night flights keep supply chains moving while cities sleep.

title: Regional Jet
body:
Regional Jet is a smaller jet airliner seating roughly fifty to one hundred passengers, built for short routes between smaller cities and airline hubs. Regional jets such as the Embraer E-Jet family connect communities that cannot fill a large airliner.

Regional jets keep small cities on the air map, and their economics made hub-and-spoke airline networks possible.

title: Wide-Body Jet
body:
Wide-Body Jet is a large jet airliner with a twin-aisle cabin, built for long-haul routes and high passenger counts. The Boeing 747, the first wide-body, entered service in 1970 and earned the name Queen of the Skies; the Airbus A380 later became the largest passenger jet ever built.

Wide-body jets made mass long-haul travel possible, and their double-deck and twin-aisle cabins are familiar to every long-distance flyer.

title: Jet Trainer
body:
Jet Trainer is a jet aircraft built to train military and civilian pilots in jet handling, usually with two seats and forgiving flight characteristics. Jet trainers are the classroom of jet aviation, where pilots learn speed, energy management, and instrument flying.

Jet trainers are a practical, unglamorous type, and every jet pilot's career passes through one.
